A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same STRUCTURE work. The complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and expanded supplementary material.

before.justification: v1 reports original image–text classification and retrieval experiments, audio–text retrieval, data-scaling studies, and ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds single-cell image–transcriptome experiments, additional comparisons, and supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: Both versions use frozen encoders, mutual-kNN layer selection, and the same multilevel Jensen–Shannon structural regularizer. Added model applications and ablations do not revise the default method. The three-modality loss in v2's Limitations illustrates a prospective extension of the existing additive regularization.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained image–text and audio–text coverage, v2 Appendix H.4 adds paired human single-cell image–transcriptome alignment, evaluated through retrieval and cell-type classification. This introduces a distinct modality pairing and biological task setting.

E2.justification: v2 Table 11 adds FuseMix as a fourth alignment method across the extended benchmark, including variants with layer selection and STRUCTURE. Table 10 also adds ASIF to the COCO/CIFAR comparison that contained only Kernel Local CKA and the proposed method in v1 Table 8.

E3.justification: New protocols include the single-cell split of 100 training and 19,800 test samples, modality-gap measurement, and controlled variations in batch size, subset selection, normalization, and similarity functions. Table 12 adds BGE-Small/Base with ViT-G and MiniLM/mpnet with ViT-T. The original COCO setup and default hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v1 Table 7 tested regularization depth, strength, and layer-selection metrics. v2 Table 9 substantially expands these controls with batch-size, fixed-versus-random subset, normalization, and distance-function ablations. Appendix H.5 additionally investigates whether alignment reduces the modality gap.

E5.justification: The new checklist explains omitted standard deviations through deterministic training with identity-initialized projections, fixed seeds, and fixed data order, and identifies error bars for nondeterministic experiments. Existing repetition counts are retained; this is additional reporting, not evidence of increased independent runs.

E6.justification: The original benchmark values are retained apart from equivalent rounding, but v2 adds extensive results for new baselines, backbone combinations, ablations, and modality-gap analysis. Its new single-cell Table 7 reports retrieval R@5 of 4.2 versus 6.0 and classification scores of 40.3 versus 52.5 for the baseline and proposed configuration.

T1.justification: The substantive mathematical definitions, Lemmas 1–3, and generalization-bound proof are retained, with the proof moving from Appendix D to C. The added random-walk intuition and illustrative three-modality sum provide explanation rather than a new theoretical result or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same two contributions, low-data alignment claims, 24-benchmark scope, and headline improvements of 51.6% for classification and 91.8% for retrieval. Additional experiments support these existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations linking the new ablations to robustness of structural preservation and reduced modality gaps to downstream performance. It replaces v1's biology-as-future-work discussion with a biological example and newly acknowledges that alignment beyond two modalities remains untested, while outlining a possible extension.

D1.justification: v2 discloses identity initialization, fixed-seed/data-order behavior, and batch-based regularizer computation, and adds a project-page link and code-release statement. Listing 1 changes its default from L=3 to L=1, resolving its disagreement with the default already stated in v1. Hardware and general training settings are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds targeted positioning relative to FuseMix and ASIF, distinguishing complementary augmentation from learning-free matching, and connects the work to earlier geometric representation-alignment research. Supporting references for cell embeddings and modality-gap analysis are also added; the overall research framing remains intact.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. Changes include localized explanations and editing, moving Limitations into the main paper, reordering two experimental discussions, expanding appendix subsections, and inserting the NeurIPS checklist.

P2.justification: The NeurIPS format changes body width, title and abstract layout, running headers, and display placement throughout. v2 adds the layerwise heatmaps in Figure 8 and biological/modality-gap Tables 7–8, substantially expands the ablation and model-comparison tables, and resizes or relocates retained displays.

improvement.justification: The added FuseMix/ASIF comparisons and controlled ablations strengthen support for the unchanged method, while the reference-code correction improves consistency. Gains are limited by reporting weaknesses: the biological dataset is insufficiently identified, Table 8 leaves unexplained distances above 2 for its stated L2-normalized modality-gap metric, and H.7 reports a 32.9% CIFAR100 gain over ASIF although Table 10 implies about 97.1%. These issues weaken parts of the new evidence without negating the useful comparison and robustness results.
